# MM-P1-L2-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1
Revision: Rev F  
Supersedes: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Related documents: ECN-2026-041, SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-04

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance tasks, required tooling, stepwise procedure, and acceptance criteria for the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 identified as EQ-P1-L2-RR01. It applies to maintenance technicians and engineers responsible for mechanical, lubrication, and fastener integrity tasks on this machine. Use this manual in conjunction with ECN-2026-041 for engineering changes and SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04 for lockout/tagout and permit requirements.

Background and rationale
Ring rolling mills operate with high contact loads and tightly controlled clearances. Fastener preload and rolling element lubrication are primary contributors to reliable operation and dimensional control. The mandrel clamp joint secures tooling that transmits large axial and bending loads; correct bolt torque is required to maintain clamp stiffness and prevent slippage or galling. Bearing lubrication frequency controls grease condition and film thickness to prevent mixed or boundary lubrication, reducing wear and risk of subsurface fatigue. The procedures below focus on controlling these root causes of failure to minimize unplanned downtime and maintain process capability.

Required tools and materials
- Torque wrench calibrated per shop practice and traceable calibration records. Use a tool capable of achieving the specified torque for the mandrel clamp bolts.  
- Socket and drive set compatible with the clamp bolt head.  
- Clean lint-free rags and approved cleaning solvent.  
- Manufacturer-approved bearing lubricant for the main roll bearings.  
- Grease gun with clean coupler and reservoirs dedicated to bearing lubricant.  
- Maintenance log forms and history folder for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P1-L2-01.

Critical values
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.  
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 175 hours.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Verify that the work area is clear of production material and that the machine is in the safe state required by SOP-P1-L2-01. Confirm electrical and mechanical isolation per SOP-P1-L2-04 before accessing clamp hardware or lubrication points.  
- Gather the tools and materials listed above. Record the equipment serial and location references in the maintenance log for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and application
- Clean the clamp bolt head and surrounding surfaces with solvent and a lint-free rag to remove debris and old lubricants. Ensure threads visible for inspection are free of contamination.  
- Position the calibrated torque wrench and socket onto the clamp bolt head. Apply torque in a smooth, continuous motion until the wrench indicates the set value. Observe wrench behavior to ensure proper seating and avoid impact-style forcing.  
- If multiple clamp bolts are present in the clamp assembly, sequence torque application using an alternating pattern to avoid introducing clamp distortion. Repeat final torque verification on all bolts after the sequence is complete.  
- Document the tool identification, torque value applied, technician name, and any anomalies such as thread damage, coating loss, or bolt elongation in the maintenance record for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm access to the bearing grease fittings and clean the fitting area to prevent contamination during lubrication. Inspect seals and housings for visible damage before lubricant application.  
- Use the approved lubricant and grease gun. Apply lubricant until a small amount is observed at the bearing seals or per bearing manufacturer guidance, taking care not to overpack. If resistance increases sharply during pumping, stop and inspect for potential blockage.  
- Record the lubricant lot number, grease quantity dispensed if measured by pump counts, and the start/stop time in the equipment lubrication log. Update the running hours counter for main roll bearing lubrication interval on the EQ-P1-L2-RR01 maintenance tracker.

Inspection and corrective actions
- After torque and lubrication tasks, perform a visual inspection of adjacent components for signs of leakage, looseness, or contamination. Rotate the mandrel or rolls slowly as required to confirm free movement without abnormal noise or binding.  
- If any component fails inspection or if bolt threads or bearing seals show damage, tag the component out of service and notify maintenance supervision and engineering per ECN-2026-041 for disposition. Record corrective actions taken and parts replaced in the equipment history.

Examples and records to keep
- Example entry for clamp torque action: specify the equipment id EQ-P1-L2-RR01, date, technician initials, tool id, applied torque 395 N·m, and observations. Attach any photographs of bolt condition.  
- Example entry for bearing lubrication: specify equipment id EQ-P1-L2-RR01, lubricant id, grease lot number, start/stop time, and note main roll bearing lubrication interval reference 175 hours. Include next due hours value in the maintenance planner.  
- Maintain a folder for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 containing torque certificates, calibration records for torque wrench, grease certification, and copies of any ECN-2026-041 change forms that affect clamp or bearing systems.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts must show no visual thread damage, must be seated flush without gaps attributable to improperly installed washers or debris, and must be verified at the specified torque value recorded as 395 N·m. Any bolt that does not reach the specified torque due to deformation or stripping must be removed and replaced prior to machine return to service.  
- Main roll bearings must show adequate lubricant presence at seals or meet manufacturer criteria after service and maintenance records must reflect the main roll bearing lubrication interval 175 hours. Bearings that exhibit elevated running noise, excess heat, or visible lubricant degradation must be escalated for bearing teardown and evaluation per ECN-2026-041.  
- All maintenance entries for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 must include technician identification, tool calibration references, and linkage to SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04 where lockout and permit actions were required.

Revision and change control
All deviations, repairs, or engineering substitutions must reference ECN-2026-041 and be recorded under the EQ-P1-L2-RR01 equipment history before returning the machine to production.
